mianliu:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: production square raster icon for an Europa Universalis IV government reform, ultimately displayed at 57 x 57 pixels.
Primary request: A single majestic Chinese ceremonial mianliu crown (冕旒冠), representing the Zhou Son of Heaven, WITHOUT a wearer or face. Three-quarter view from slightly above, showing a broad rectangular horizontal crown board, the compact crown body underneath, and clearly separated hanging white jade bead strands from the front and rear edges. The silhouette must read immediately as a ceremonial crown, not a European crown or military helmet.
Style: richly rendered painterly three-dimensional historical strategy-game object icon, tactile lacquer, restrained metal and jade material highlights; dignified, solemn and restrained.
Palette: deep lacquer black crown body and board, restrained vermilion red lining and ribbon accents, luminous ivory-white jade beads, very small muted gold fittings. No dominant gold.
Composition: tightly framed single crown, centered, fills roughly 85 percent of square, every part fully inside frame. No person, no head, no pedestal, no additional ritual objects. Strong clean crown-board silhouette and legible separated bead strands; simplify tiny ornament so this remains recognizable when reduced to 57 pixels. No busy filigree.
Backdrop and light: dark cool blue-green charcoal softly painted background, subtle lighter diffuse area behind black crown, controlled warm edge highlights separate board and body from background. No magical halo or luminous magic. Keep red accents compact.
No text, glyphs, lettering, symbols, caption, watermark, frame, border, UI, collage or multiple panels. Generate one finished square icon image.
